hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this variable because `HPrimeIsoHOver`, used in `HPrimeIsoRestrictedResolutionSectionsHomology`, depends on it. But Mathlib already provides it as a global instance. `GrothendieckTopology.HasSheafCompose` is a `Prop` class (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Whiskering.lean:43). The instance `hasSheafCompose_of_preservesLimitsOfSize` (Whiskering.lean:159) gives `J.HasSheafCompose F` from `[PreservesLimitsOfSize.{v₁, max u₁ v₁} F]`. For `C = Opens X` with `X : TopCat.{u}`, both u₁ and v₁ are `u`, so it needs `PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u,u} (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})`. That is `AddCommGrpCat.forget_preservesLimitsOfSize`, the `to_additive` version of `CommGrpCat.forget_preservesLimitsOfSize`, which holds for arbitrary universes (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Limits.lean:404). The higher-priority `hasSheafCompose_of_preservesMulticospan` also applies through the same preservation instance. The sibling library confirms that synthesis works: SchemeProperties/IdealSheafModule.lean:54 uses `GrothendieckTopology.HasSheafCompose.isSheaf` for `(Opens.grothendieckTopology X)` and `forget AddCommGrpCat` with no such hypothesis in scope. If the variable is deleted (e.g. with `omit ... in`), every occurrence in the statement and in the lemmas the proof calls (`HPrimeEquivHOver_naturality`, `restrictedAcyclicResolution_extPositiveIsoHomology_hom_naturality_assoc`, `restrictedResolutionHomComplexIsoSectionsHomology_hom_naturality`, …) is elaborated with the same global instance. Since the class is a Prop, the statement is unchanged up to proof irrelevance, and the same proof goes through. This can be deleted independently of the over-site instance below; both can also be deleted together.

Same argument for the over-site. `Over ((Opens.map f).obj V)` is a category whose objects live in `Type u` and whose morphisms live in universe `u`. So `hasSheafCompose_of_preservesLimitsOfSize` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Whiskering.lean:159) again needs only `PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u,u} (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})`. `AddCommGrpCat.forget_preservesLimitsOfSize` (Grp/Limits.lean:404, `to_additive`) provides it for all universe levels. Hence `((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over W).HasSheafCompose (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})` is synthesized globally. `HasSheafCompose` is a `Prop` class, so after deleting the variable the statement, which needs the instance through `HPrimeIsoHOver` / `restrictToOver` / `HPrimeIsoRestrictedResolutionSectionsHomology`, elaborates to a proof-irrelevantly identical term. The lemmas used in the proof pick up the same global instance, so the proof works unchanged.
